learn.title: An ordered tree
learn.body: A binary search tree, or BST, adds one rule to a binary tree. For every node, everything in its left subtree is smaller, and everything in its right subtree is larger. A subtree is a node together with all it leads to.

learn.title: Why the rule helps
learn.body: To find a value, compare it with the root. If it is smaller, the answer can only be on the left, so the whole right side is ignored. Each step skips a large part of the tree, much as a binary search skips half of a sorted array.

learn.title: Building from 5, 3, 8, 1, 4
learn.body: Insert the values one at a time into an empty tree.
steps: 3 is less than 5, so it goes left of 5. 8 goes right
1 is less than 5, then less than 3, so it is left of 3
4 is less than 5, then greater than 3, so it is right of 3

learn.title: The smallest value
learn.body: The smallest value is far left: keep going left until there is no left child.
The same values inserted in a different order can give a differently shaped tree.

questions.prompt: In a BST, where do smaller values go relative to a node?
questions.explanation: Left is smaller, right is larger.

questions.prompt: A node holds 10. Its right subtree may contain...
questions.explanation: The rule is the same for every node.

questions.prompt: A BST holds 5, 3, 8, 1, 4. What is its smallest value?
questions.explanation: Go left from the root: 5, 3, 1. Node 1 has no left child.

questions.prompt: You look for 4 in the tree with root 5. What do you do first?
choices: Go left, because 4 is less than 5
questions.explanation: 4 is smaller than 5, so it can only be in the left subtree.

questions.prompt: Which tree is NOT a valid BST?
choices: Root 5 with 3 as its left child
Root 5 with 8 as its right child
Root 5 with 6 as its left child
questions.explanation: 6 is larger than 5, so it cannot be on the left.

questions.prompt: To find the largest value in a BST, keep going \_\_.
questions.explanation: Larger values are on the right, so the largest has no right child.
